title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-market-scanner-followups-followups review (PR #239)
description: Non-blocking findings from the pr-reviewer pass on PR #239 (the typed `Retry-After` OpenAPI header added to POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run's and POST /api/ibkr/breadth/snapshot's 429 responses), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: The generated `"Retry-After"?: number` field on both 429 responses (frontend/src/api/types.ts) is currently unreachable from any actual frontend code: the hand-rolled frontend/src/api/client.ts `request()`/`ApiError` never surfaces `response.headers` to callers at all (`ApiError` only carries `status`/`detail`). Before any future feature actually reads Retry-After to schedule a UI retry, thread response headers through the client (or a dedicated typed accessor) -- and note that a real `Headers` instance is read via `.get('Retry-After')` (returns a string) rather than bracket access on a plain object, so the generated `number` type needs an explicit parse step, not a direct cast.

The `Retry-After` header spec in backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py's `responses={}` (both routes) omits `required: true`, even though `_rate_limited_http_exception` unconditionally sets this header on every 429 these two routes raise. Add `required: true` so the generated type is `"Retry-After": number` (non-optional) instead of `"Retry-After"?: number`, and regenerate backend/openapi.json + frontend/src/api/types.ts.

The `headers: {"Retry-After": {...}}` dict literal (and its enclosing 429 `description` string) is duplicated verbatim between run_ibkr_scanner's and record_ibkr_breadth_snapshot's `responses={}` in backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py. Factor it into a shared module-level constant (e.g. `_RETRY_AFTER_HEADER_SPEC`) referenced by both routes' `responses={}` dicts so the two 429 specs can't silently drift out of sync.

decisions.decision: Added `retryAfterSeconds: number | null` as a new field on `ApiError` (frontend/src/api/client.ts), populated only for a non-2xx response via a new `parseRetryAfterSeconds()` helper that reads `response.headers.get('Retry-After')` and accepts only a digits-only integer-seconds string (the form these two backend routes always send), returning `null` otherwise -- including for an RFC 9110-legal HTTP-date `Retry-After` value, which no route in this app ever actually sends. Rejected alternatives: (1) a separate `getResponseHeaders()`/typed accessor threaded alongside the parsed body through `request()`'s return value, which would force every one of the ~30 existing `ApiError` call sites across api/*.ts and their tests to change shape for a header only two routes ever set; (2) casting the header string directly to `number` per the generated OpenAPI type, which is simply wrong for a real `Headers.get()` return value (always `string | null`) and would produce `NaN`/type-lies for a non-numeric header.
decisions.rationale: This is the narrowest change that actually makes Retry-After reachable from frontend code (closing the checklist's core gap) without reshaping `request()`'s generic success-path return type or every existing caller. `retryAfterSeconds` defaults to `null` on the constructor and every other error path (network failure, 4xx/5xx without the header), so no existing test asserting on `status`/`detail` needed to change.

decisions.decision: Factored the duplicated 429 `responses={}` entry (description + `headers` dict, now with `required: true` added) into a single module-level `_RETRY_AFTER_429_RESPONSE` dict in backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py, referenced by both `run_ibkr_scanner` and `record_ibkr_breadth_snapshot`'s `responses={}`, rather than the checklist's suggested name `_RETRY_AFTER_HEADER_SPEC` (which described only the inner `headers` sub-dict, not the full 429 entry that was actually duplicated including its `description` and `model`).
decisions.rationale: Factoring the whole 429 entry (not just the `headers` sub-dict) is what actually prevents the two specs from drifting -- the checklist's own repro line named the `description` string as also duplicated. The renamed constant reflects what it actually holds.

review.notes: Full review: backend pytest (1135 passed, 99.95% coverage), frontend vitest (707 passed, 99.72%/99.19%/99.72%/99.78% stmt/branch/func/line coverage) -- both well above the 90% gate and no regression. ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc all clean; check_profit_target_wording.py clean. Regenerated backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts from scratch and confirmed zero diff against the committed snapshot -- genuinely in sync, not just claimed. Both recorded decisions are sound: the ApiError.retryAfterSeconds field is the narrower backward-compatible choice over threading headers through request()'s return type, and the _RETRY_AFTER_429_RESPONSE constant name accurately reflects that the whole 429 entry (not just the headers sub-dict the checklist's suggested name implied) was duplicated. Verified _rate_limited_http_exception unconditionally sets Retry-After as a digits-only integer string on both call sites, so required: true and the frontend regex parse are both honest. Verified (via FastAPI's own get_openapi_path source) that sharing one _RETRY_AFTER_429_RESPONSE dict object across two routes' responses={} is safe -- FastAPI deepcopies each entry before mutating, so no aliasing hazard. No UI surface touched (only api/client.ts and api/types.ts; the new field is deliberately unreachable from any UI code yet per the task's own decision) -- browser walkthrough and e2e suite both explicitly skipped as not applicable. area is backend/api (not signals/portfolio) and skill is null, so verify-elder-signal skipped; no new module/dependency/layer, so architecture-review skipped; no frontend component touched, so the 7a placement check doesn't apply. Independent code-review skill pass (medium effort) found zero correctness/reuse/simplification/efficiency issues, independently corroborating the FastAPI deepcopy finding. No blocking or non-blocking findings -- no follow-up task filed this round.

Confirmed FastAPI's get_openapi_path deepcopies each responses={} entry before mutating (process_response = copy.deepcopy(additional_response)), so sharing _RETRY_AFTER_429_RESPONSE across both routes has no aliasing hazard.
